subject: Many shiny apps through Apache proxy and websocket blockage

messages.author: 69658a5d047f38b4
messages.subject: Many shiny apps through Apache proxy and websocket blockage
parts:
Hi,

I have shiny-server configured as follows:

server {
  listen 3838;
  location / {
    site_dir /srv/shiny-server-public;
    log_dir /var/log/shiny-server-public;
    directory_index on;
  }
}

shiny-server 1.2.3.368
R 3.1.0
shiny 0.10.2.1
Ubuntu 14.04.1 LTS (GNU/Linux 3.13.0-39-generic x86_64)

From `/srv/shiny-server-public` I have symbolic links to apps located in various users' home directories (in case that matters).
This `server1.obs-vlfr.fr` serves apps on the local network but is not accessible from outside. All apps work fine and quickly in this configuration.

`server2` is accessible from the internet and runs Apache. A proxy is configured to point to `server1.obs-vlfr.fr:3838` this way

ProxyPass  /data/view         http://server1.obs-vlfr.fr:3838/
ProxyPassReverse  /data/view  http://server1.obs-vlfr.fr:3838/
RedirectMatch permanent ^/data/view$ /data/view/

This results in:
http://www.obs-vlfr.fr/data/view/
giving access to all shiny apps on `server1`. The apps of significance are: 
http://www.obs-vlfr.fr/data/view/dyfamed/ctd/
http://www.obs-vlfr.fr/data/view/dyfamed/uvp/
http://www.obs-vlfr.fr/data/view/eol/ctd/
http://www.obs-vlfr.fr/data/view/eol/surface/
http://www.obs-vlfr.fr/data/view/radehydro/ctd/
http://www.obs-vlfr.fr/data/view/radehydro/std/
http://www.obs-vlfr.fr/data/view/radezoo/wp2/

When I try to run them all at once in a browser window (Safari or Chrome, latest versions, on OS X):
- everything seems slower
- a couple of them (usually among the last ones started) show the UI but never show the plots
- some of them may also grey out or become unresponsive.
I imagine this will be worse when we make these URLs known and get a few concurrent users.

The only error I can spot in the Javascript console is: 

WebSocket connection to 'ws://www.obs-vlfr.fr/data/view/radehydro/std/__sockjs__/926/xdfaovb8/websocket' failed: Error during WebSocket handshake: Unexpected response code: 400

I've read that websocket errors are common with such a proxied config. I've also read that this should not be a problem because shiny should fallback on another solution when websockets are not available. Yet, the last couple of apps that are stuck show a "Waiting for websocket" message in the bottom info bar in Chrome and get unstuck when I close a few of the first apps. When an app loads, I get very long load times on a "resource" called xhr_streaming, which seems to be related to proxying also.

So my questions are:
- what is the preferred/recommended (Apache) proxying configuration?
- is there a limit on the number of apps ran simultaneously by shiny-server (free)?
- is there a limit on the number of websockets/websockets emulations?
- what can I do, overall, to make this work?

Thank you very much in advance for your insight!

PS: By the way, for those who are curious, these apps allow us to showcase the large monitoring data sets that have been collected by my institution since as early as 1957, some on a daily basis. Combining the easy and fast filtering + computation of dplyr, the power of ggplot2 and the interactivity of shiny made these apps possible, even easy (once I got the hang of it). So thank you very very much Joe, Hadley and all of the great talent concentrated at RStudio! Now I just need the final step to make this work public.

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Many shiny apps through Apache proxy and websocket blockage
parts:
The problem is almost certainly the number of HTTP (not WebSocket) connections originating from a single browser. I'll hazard a guess that the websocket connection is actually failing due to the Apache proxy, so your browser is falling back to regular HTTP connections.

By default, Chrome will only let 6 simultaneous HTTP connections be made to a given server (or maybe server/port combination? not sure). If six simultaneous connections are already in progress then any additional requests will have to wait until a previous one completes.

You can test this by opening Firefox, you should see that even when the last few Chrome tabs are stuck, Firefox should be able to open new tabs.

BTW, the WebSocket connection limit for browsers is different (higher) than HTTP connections, that's why I suspect the websockets are failing.

parts:
Apparently, my reply (through email) never made it to the group. Here it is again:

This is indeed the case, there is a cap per browser which seems to be at 6 for Chrome, Safari and Firefox. This is consistent with the answer to that stack overflow question: http://stackoverflow.com/questions/985431/max-parallel-http-connections-in-a-browser

This may be a problem since I expect people to browse these apps side by side.

It seems the solution would be to get web sockets through the proxy. In addition, a few timing tests seem to show that the http fallback is slower than the web sockets (by 20 to 30%). I guess this is expected.

Is there a solution know to work with shiny-server (I would think of mod_proxy_wstunnel but before annoying my IT guys with this it would be nice to know if this has been working for someone and what ws:// address was proxied exactly).
